input.name: Dollar Store Sessions
input.tagline: Parkdale's 650-cap room for the indie acts that outgrew the Baby G.
input.audience: Parkdale's top venues skew 25–34 (25 29 and 30 34 tags in 32 and 31 of the top 40 venues), and the area leans 35–44 in the demographic check. The crowd is Groups of Friends, Young Professionals, Foodies, Cocktail Enthusiasts and Art Enthusiasts. They like Stylish, Hip and Boutique places, and their local favourites are Arkells, July Talk, Kevin Drew and Maylee Todd, plus brands such as blogTO and the Art Gallery of Ontario.
input.gap: Qloo shows one live music venue within 1.2 km: The Baby G, an intimate, industrial room about 1 km away in Little Portugal. Nothing mid-size sits on Queen West itself. A 6,000 sq ft room (about 667 guests) fills the step up for acts too big for the Baby G, with drinks serious enough for Cocktail and Wine Enthusiasts.
input.offer: Ticketed shows at $20–40, with a free early-evening listening set. The bar serves draft and craft beer, a short cocktail list and wine by the glass at $9–16, and coffee and tea plus specialty non-alcoholic drinks (Greenhouse juices) at the daytime and early-set bar. Standing room on the floor, with a few high tables and bar stools.

design_choices.choice: The raised stage sits against the back wall at centre, at the end of the 25–30 m hall, so sightlines run clear down the room. The row of columns is used for standing high tables, not blocking the floor. The bar is in the foreground on the left wall, as far from the stage as the room allows.

Walnut slat panels with felt backing replace the grey slatwall, and charcoal acoustic panelling covers the back wall. The existing ceiling is kept and painted dark. Polished concrete floors keep the look Modern with an Industrial edge, echoing the Baby G's Industrial tag.

design_choices.element: Design tags swapped after the audience check
design_choices.choice: Eclectic, Quirky, Lively, Cozy, Social and Energetic were marked mismatch because they pull a 55+ female crowd away from the local 35–44 skew. They are replaced by Modern (fits), Stylish (fits) and Intimate and Industrial (neutral). The look is a restrained, stylish room, and the energy comes from the bands.
Black track lights and pendant globes replace the fluorescent tubes. Warm amber stage light gives a stylish, intimate feel on the floor.
The long walnut bar leads with beer, cocktails and wine, backed by coffee and tea and a non-alcoholic list.

House playlists use local favourites between sets: July Talk, Arkells, Kevin Drew and Maylee Todd. Posters and promotion go through blogTO and Narcity, and a gallery-style poster wall nods to the Art Gallery of Ontario.

programming.why: Highest-affinity act in the slate (0.962) and just under the 0.94 popularity cap, so it can fill a 667-cap room.
Strong affinity (0.952) with fans of Sneaky Dee's and The Baby G, and a popularity of 0.904 that suits the room.
A seated-feel, early-set night for the Couples and Foodies crowd, at popularity 0.832.
A relaxed Sunday show for the Relaxing, Romantic and Welcoming crowd.
At popularity 0.708, a lower-risk act to build a midweek habit with 25–34s.
Adds an art-forward night for Art Enthusiasts and the Parkdale arts crowd.

risks: The audience check shows the area skews 35–44 and the local venue set is dining-led, so weeknight attendance depends on programming that appeals to both the 25–34 and 35–44 groups.
Qloo found only one comparable live venue (The Baby G), so the demand evidence is thin. Test with a few pop-up nights before committing to a long lease.
A 667-capacity room needs fire, noise and licensing approval for an ex-retail unit, and the drop ceiling needs acoustic work. Rent is an illustrative $18–26k a month.
